# Breaking Down The NBA Schedule For Fantasy Basketball

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-16, 33:30. https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls

## Summary

Josh Lloyd goes through the newly released NBA schedule and explains which parts matter for fantasy and which don't. Because of the new tanking rules and lottery reform, he now recommends ending fantasy playoffs on March 28. He also says leagues should merge the NBA Cup half weeks and the All-Star weeks. In his view, differences in total back-to-backs (three games across the season), total playoff games and quality games are too small to change draft decisions. Playoff back-to-backs matter a little more. His main point is that two-game weeks in the fantasy playoffs are what really count. Minnesota has one in mid-March that most playoff formats can't avoid, which should drop Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball a little. Cleveland, Charlotte, Dallas and New Orleans also have two-game weeks, depending on when your league ends.

## Rules and methods

- [1:28](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=88) Before you look at any schedule, check your league settings and playoff dates.
  > "That's the number one thing with any any question that you're doing in any fantasy league."
- [2:30](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150) The playoff schedule should only break ties between similar players. It should not drive your draft philosophy.
  > "And if you are talking just tie breakers behind between players, then sure, no problem."
- [3:07](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=187) Player value is uncertain. Players picked around 100 often finish around 30, and players picked around 20 can finish around 60. Don't stack your roster based on playoff game counts.
  > "every year a player that was picked 100th becomes 30th. Player that was picked 20th becomes"
- [4:55](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=295) In roto leagues, play to the end of the season. Fantasy playoff schedule details don't matter there.
  > "If you're playing in a roto league, none of this fantasy playoff stuff matters to you at all."
- [6:12](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=372) Because of the tanking rule changes and lottery reform, the speaker expects less resting late in the season, so leagues can end a week later than before.
  > "given the the change in the tanking rules and the lottery reform, I actually think we could push it back a week."
- [7:15](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=435) His recommended end date for fantasy playoffs is March 28 (matchup 21), with a standard 3-week playoff.
  > "is to end on March the 28th. So, I am pushing it back a week."
- [9:26](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=566) Merge the two NBA Cup half weeks (November 30 to December 13) into one 14-day matchup. Also merge the All-Star weeks.
  > "That'll start week seven and I think that should be combined into one matchup over 14 days."
- [13:31](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=811) The difference in total back-to-backs between teams is small (16 at most, 13 at fewest), so don't overweight it.
  > "The difference in backto-backs is 16 for the most and 13 for the fewest."
- [14:53](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=893) Back-to-backs during the fantasy playoffs matter more than the season total.
  > "And what is more important is playoff backto-backs."
- [17:38](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1058) Most back-to-back problems come from players returning from in-season injuries, and nobody can predict those.
  > "if someone gets hurt in season and comes back, they sit a few back tobacks."
- [21:26](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286) Two-game weeks in the fantasy playoffs are bad. This is the schedule factor that actually matters.
  > "Two game weeks, they are bad. That there is in the fantasy playoffs, two game weeks are bad."
- [22:41](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1361) A top-two seed with a first-round bye can absorb an early two-game playoff week.
  > "So, if you are hyper confident you're going to be a top two seed and your league has a buy"
- [25:22](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1522) If an early pick with a two-game playoff week falls late enough with no better option, take him. Don't reach for him early.
  > "But if you're debating it at six, seven, don't do it."
- [27:45](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1665) In head-to-head leagues, categories or points, a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board.
  > "If you're playing head-to-head leagues, doesn't matter if it's categories or points, it doesn't matter. The twoame week has to drop somebody down."
- [28:43](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1723) A quality game is one played on a day with few games, so you don't face start/sit decisions. The cutoff should be 11 games (or 10), not Basketball Monster's default of 5.
  > "The cutoff should be either 11 or 10. I actually think 11 is probably right."
- [29:07](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1747) Quality game totals vary too little between teams to affect draft decisions.
  > "the range of games here if I use 11 as a cut off is between 65 and 70."
- [29:57](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1797) Schedule quirks (back-to-backs, playoff games, two-game weeks) only matter for your first three rounds of players.
  > "unless it's your first three round players. That's it. So, like I said,"
- [31:29](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1889) Injuries peak early in the season because preseason and training camp are short. They drop off by mid-December. The late-season spike should be smaller this year because there should be fewer fake injuries.
  > "So, you will get peak injuries. By the time you hit mid December, it all drops"
- [32:38](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1958) Don't agonize over 12 versus 11 playoff games because too much can change.
  > "Don't agonize over 12 games versus 11 games in your fantasy playoffs because so many things can change."
